intro: The language between a charging station and the server that runs it, the CSMS (charging station management system). The charger keeps one WebSocket open and sends JSON messages: who it is, the state of its connectors, which card wants to charge, and the meter during each charge. The CSMS answers every message, and can send requests of its own on the same connection.

connect.title: Connect
connect.text: The charger opens a secure WebSocket to its CSMS. The connection stays open, so either side can send at any time.

boot.title: Boot
boot.text: The first message after power-up says who the charger is. The CSMS accepts it, gives the time and sets the heartbeat interval. Then the charger reports each connector: connector 1 is Available.

authorize.title: Tap a card
authorize.text: A driver holds an RFID card to the reader. The charger asks the CSMS whether this card may charge. It may.

start.title: Start
start.text: The car is plugged in and starts to take energy. The charger opens a transaction and sends the meter reading at its start.

charge.title: Meter values
charge.text: While the car charges, the charger sends the meter every 15 minutes. The CSMS sees the energy grow.

stop.title: Stop
stop.text: The driver taps the card again. The transaction ends after one hour and 11040 Wh. The CSMS can now bill it.

frames.boot: I am an AC-22 from ExampleVendor, just powered up
frames.boot-conf: Accepted. Here is the time; heartbeat every 300 s
frames.started-conf: Noted, the card is still Accepted

notes.upgrade: Inside TLS, the charger asks to turn this HTTP connection into a WebSocket. The address ends in its identity, CS-0042. The header Sec-WebSocket-Protocol asks for ocpp2.0.1, and HTTP Basic authentication carries the charger's password.
notes.switch: The CSMS agrees and names the subprotocol it chose: ocpp2.0.1. From now on both sides send WebSocket frames, each with one OCPP message in JSON.
notes.status: A CALL with timestamp, connectorStatus Available, evseId 1 and connectorId 1. An EVSE is one charging point; it can have several connectors.
notes.status-conf: A CALLRESULT with an empty payload: [3,"1002",{}]. Every CALL gets an answer, even when there is nothing to say.
notes.authorize: idToken 04A2B3C4D5E6F7, type ISO14443: the 7-byte serial number of the RFID card. Many chargers also keep a local list of cards, to decide without asking.
notes.authorize-conf: idTokenInfo with status Accepted. Other answers, such as Blocked, Expired, Invalid or Unknown, mean the charger must not start.
notes.started: eventType Started, triggerReason ChargingStateChanged, seqNo 0. The charger picks the transactionId, TX-0187. The event carries the card's idToken, chargingState Charging, and a meter value with context Transaction.Begin: 12840 Wh.
notes.started-conf: The event carried the card, so the answer carries its status again: idTokenInfo Accepted.
notes.updated: eventType Updated, triggerReason MeterValuePeriodic, seqNo 1, with two readings: the energy register and the power. The playground shows the whole message.
notes.updated-conf: An empty payload: the CSMS has nothing to add.
notes.ended: eventType Ended, triggerReason StopAuthorized, seqNo 2, stoppedReason Local, chargingState EVConnected (the cable is still in), and the last meter value with context Transaction.End: 23880 Wh.
notes.ended-conf: An empty payload. The CSMS bills 23880 − 12840 = 11040 Wh to the card's owner.

ws-text.name: FIN · opcode
ws-text.note: 0x81: the FIN bit (0x80) says the whole message is in this frame. Opcode 0x1 says it is text, UTF-8.

ws-mask-126.name: Mask · length
ws-mask-126.note: 0xFE: the mask bit (0x80) is set, because a client must mask what it sends. The rest, 126 (0x7E), says the length follows in 2 bytes.

ws-len-170.name: Length
ws-len-170.note: 0x00AA = 170 bytes of JSON follow. The playground shows them.

ws-key.name: Masking key
ws-key.note: 4 random bytes. Each byte of the JSON is XORed with them in turn: "[" (0x5B) travels as 0x61. This is not encryption; TLS does that.

ws-len-88.name: Length
ws-len-88.note: 0x58 = 88 bytes of JSON follow. The mask bit is 0, because a server never masks, so no masking key follows.

a-type.name: MessageTypeId
a-type.note: 2 is a CALL, a request. Its answer is a 3 (CALLRESULT) or a 4 (CALLERROR).

a-id.name: MessageId
a-id.note: Picked by the sender, unique on this connection. The answer carries the same id; nothing else ties the two together.

a-action.name: Action
a-action.note: Which message this is. An answer has no action: its id tells which CALL it answers.

a-payload.name: Payload
a-payload.note: The request itself, a JSON object. Its fields are checked against the JSON schema of BootNotificationRequest.

facts.standard: OCPP 2.0.1 (Open Charge Alliance, 2020). OCPP 1.6J is still common.
facts.between: Charging station → CSMS (charging station management system)
facts.transport: WebSocket (RFC 6455) over TLS, subprotocol ocpp2.0.1: one JSON message per text frame
facts.security: TLS. Security profile 2 adds a password (HTTP Basic), profile 3 a client certificate.

tips: If the CSMS does not answer with the subprotocol the charger asked for, the charger must close the connection. "It connects, then drops" is often this.
Send one CALL at a time and wait for its answer, or a timeout, before the next. A second CALL sent too early may be lost.
When a transaction starts is a setting (TxStartPoint): at plug-in, at authorization, or when energy flows. Agree on it with the CSMS team, or transactions look too long or too short.
Timestamps are UTC. Set the charger's clock from currentTime in the BootNotification answer, or meter values land in the wrong tariff period.

anatomy.call: One OCPP message: a JSON array of four parts

playground.file: A message from this lesson, as the charger sends it, laid out for reading. On the wire it is one line with no spaces.
playground.call: 2: a CALL, a request that expects an answer.
playground.message-id: The message id. The CSMS's answer carries the same one.
playground.action: The action: which message this is. Its payload follows.
playground.reason: Why the charger booted: PowerUp. Others are FirmwareUpdate, RemoteReset, Watchdog and more.
playground.model: model and vendorName are the only required fields of chargingStation.
playground.firmware: The firmware that runs now. The CSMS uses it to plan updates.
playground.event-type: Started, Updated or Ended. One transaction has exactly one Started and one Ended.
playground.timestamp: UTC, with Z. It is the time of the event, not of sending: an event stored while offline keeps its time.
playground.trigger: Why this event was sent: the meter interval (TxUpdatedInterval) has passed.
playground.seq: seqNo counts the events of this transaction from 0. A gap tells the CSMS that a message is missing.
playground.transaction-id: Chosen by the charger at the start. Every event of this charge carries it.
playground.charging-state: Charging: energy flows. Other states are EVConnected, SuspendedEV, SuspendedEVSE and Idle.
playground.energy: 15600 Wh on the meter's register, like the counter of a home meter. It does not restart at 0 for a new transaction.
playground.measurand: What was measured. Without a measurand, a value means Energy.Active.Import.Register.
playground.unit: Wh, the default unit for energy.
playground.power: 11040 W: 16 A on each of 3 phases at 230 V.
